claims.text: The Line was announced as a 170 km linear city.
Bloomberg reported (Apr 2024) only about 2.4 km of The Line expected by 2030 and fewer than 300,000 residents.
Semafor reported (22 May 2026) that NEOM halted work on The Line until at least after 2030, citing unnamed sources.
Reuters reported (about 4 Oct 2026, two sources) that the NEOM stadium was shelved indefinitely; no official announcement.
PIF governor said completing The Line by 2030 'would be good to have, but it's not a must'.
A straight, narrow cleared corridor crosses the area; at least 21.9 km long inside the 10 m frame; absent in 2020-21, faint in 2022, clear from 2023.
A dark segment about 1.5 km long: absent in Oct 2022 and 2023, present in Oct 2024, 2025 and 2026.
In 2024-2026 the dark segment is water-like in near-infrared (NDWI above zero, very low near-infrared); not in 2022-2023.
The dark segment may be standing water in a long, narrow excavation.
The dark segment has about the same length in Oct 2025 and Oct 2026; no visible extension of the corridor at 10 m.
Dezeen reported (Nov 2025) aerial photos of large, repetitive worker housing in the NEOM area.
The Wall Street Journal reported (Mar 2025) more than 50 billion dollars spent on NEOM.
Sentinel-2 images the ground at 10 m per pixel in its visible and near-infrared bands, so features narrower than about 10 m are not resolved.
Seven Sentinel-2 scenes, same orbit and season, each October from 2020 to 2026.
Soar's analysis reported (Jun 2023) a faint straight earthwork in satellite imagery of the site.
Two settlement-like complexes near the ends of the frame grow between 2020 and 2024; what they are is unknown.
Sentinel-2 revisits a given site about every five days with two or three satellites.
